capabilities.target: CRM customer account record (any customer, by email or account id)

instructions.note: The agent is explicitly permitted to look up any customer by email or account id, not just the account associated with the inbound requester, enabling IDOR-style cross-customer access.
The sole control preventing disclosure of another customer's data to the wrong party is a single prompt line, with no structural credential scoping or recipient check backing it.
'Routine' is undefined, so the model alone decides which tickets bypass any human involvement before an irreversible send.

The instruction to act immediately unless the customer is angry pushes toward fast autonomous sending, while the no-share rule assumes the model reliably resists social-engineering pressure in the same ticket, with no independent check.

controls.name: System prompt rule: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to comply with a single prompt line under adversarial pressure (e.g., a customer claiming to need another account's info); a more capable or longer-context model rationalizes exceptions or is bypassed by indirect injection, per control_decay.md.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging does not depend on model behavior and does not decay, but it is purely detective: it records a disclosure after it has already left the boundary and only helps if the log is reviewed.

controls.name: Per-requester scoped CRM credential (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to the verified requester's own record would make cross-customer reads structurally impossible regardless of model behavior; it is not present today.

controls.name: Recipient bound to system-of-record contact address (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the send destination to the address on file in the CRM record, rather than letting the model choose a free-text recipient, would sever the exfiltration path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before sending account-specific data (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: A structural approval gate with raw_action review would require a human to see the actual recipient and payload before send; none exists today, since the only gating logic is the model's own judgment of whether the customer is angry.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted ticket drives arbitrary-customer CRM read and unreviewed send via shared credentials

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email requests lookup of an arbitrary account by email or account id, per prompt.md line 3 ('You may look up any customer by email or account id').
Agent calls get_customer using CRM_SVC_TOKEN, which per runtime notes can read every customer record, returning confidential account data for the targeted (possibly unrelated) customer.

Agent drafts and sends the response directly (prompt.md line 5) using MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account that can send to any address, with no check that the recipient matches the account on file.

threat_refs.name: Privileged Tool Invocation via Prompt Manipulation
Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string in the deployment config changes; per runtime notes the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so subject.model.swappable is true and this trigger can occur silently.

evidence.observation: Agent reads the customer's own email and is told it 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' i.e. lookup is not restricted to the requester's own account.
'If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' — email send proceeds without human review by default.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you' is the only control against cross-customer disclosure, and it is a prompt instruction with no structural backing.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both called with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN); no per-request scoping or identity binding is visible in config.
'CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record' confirms credential_scope: broad for cap.crm_read.

'MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address' confirms is_egress and shared_service_account credential_scope for cap.email_send, with no recipient confirmation bound to the account record.

'The model is configured through an environment variable and is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review' — the one preventive control (ctrl.prompt_no_share) is dependent and decays under exactly this unreviewed model_upgrade path.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM access per request to the authenticated requester's own account (e.g., verify ticket requester identity via an authenticated channel and issue short-lived tokens scoped to that record) instead of a static service token with full read of all records.
Bind the outbound recipient address to the verified contact on file in the CRM record and reject sends to any address not on file, rather than letting the model choose a free-text destination.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any outbound send that includes account or billing data, at minimum for first-contact threads or recipient/account mismatches.
Alert on outbound emails where the recipient address does not match the inbound sender address, in addition to passive SIEM logging.
Tighten the system prompt to require an explicit identity-verification question before disclosing any account-specific data, understanding this only narrows, not severs, the path.

rating.rationale: A single present finding (f1.lethal_trifecta) dominates: an untrusted customer email can direct lookup of any customer's confidential account record via a broadly-scoped CRM credential, then trigger an unreviewed send through a shared mail credential capable of reaching any address. The only preventive control is a dependent prompt instruction (ctrl.prompt_no_share), which caps residual at high rather than the critical inherent tier; it is expected to fail under a model upgrade, which the design already permits without a separate review (subject.model.swappable: true), so the forecast returns to critical. No findings reach beyond this chain given the two declared capabilities.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no transcripts or execution logs were reviewed.

No identity-verification or ticketing system documentation was provided, so it is unknown whether any mechanism binds the inbound email's From address to the CRM account beyond what the model itself checks; the autonomy and trust-level classifications are inferred from prompt text at medium-to-high confidence.

No MCP server-side authorization, pinning, or rate-limiting configuration was provided; peer_identity_verified and definitions_pinned are recorded as false because no evidence of either was present, which is a conservative inference rather than a confirmed negative.

No explicit runtime step or time limits were provided for autonomy.max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes; both are recorded as null per the rubric's modifier rule rather than a confirmed absence of limits.
